messages:
olivia: quick heads-up: i'm going to land a terraform refactor that hoists provider blocks to the repo root and consolidates provider pins into a single registry. planning a staging apply later today, would like eyes for any state/alias gotchas
matt: thanks — couple quick q's: are we changing resource addresses or just moving provider config? will we need explicit `terraform state mv` ops?
olivia: not renaming resources. moving provider config to root and adding aliases where needed. for modules that relied on implicit inheritance i'll pass providers explicitly via `providers = { aws = aws }` so addresses remain stable
samir: noted. two potential issues: 1) the .terraform.lock.hcl will change (provider checksums/version bumps), 2) some modules have stricter `required_providers` ranges and might conflict. did you update module constraints?
olivia: i relaxed a couple internal modules from exact ranges to `~> 3.0` and documented which ones in the PR. expecting `terraform init` to rewrite the lockfile — i've added notes in the PR about verifying the new checksums
jane: for the lockfile: we should gate checksum changes in CI and fail the build unless someone reviews. sneaky provider upgrades in staging are a PITA
olivia: agreed. added a CI gate that diffs the lockfile against main and fails. snippet in PR: 

```bash
# ci/terraform-validate-lockfile.sh
git fetch origin main:main
if ! git diff --quiet main -- .terraform.lock.hcl; then
  echo "LOCKFILE_CHANGED"
  exit 1
fi
```

matt: also watch for plugin caching on our runners — if a runner has cached provider plugins, local plans can pass while fresh envs fail unless we mirror artifacts
samir: also watch multi-account setups. some modules rely on aliased providers (eg aws.us-west, aws.prod). when hoisting make sure alias names are preserved and are passed into module calls, otherwise terraform may try to create new provider configs in module scope
olivia: yep. i added a tflint rule to warn on implicit providers in module blocks and i'm prepping a tiny migration script that inserts the provider map into module calls automatically where safe
jane: rollback plan if staging apply does something unexpected?
olivia: manual rollback: snapshot statefile, revert the module refactor branch, run `terraform init` and use `terraform state mv` to move resources back if needed. i'll also do a dry-run in an isolated TF_DATA_DIR to inspect create/delete deltas: 

```bash
export TF_DATA_DIR=/tmp/tfdata-check
terraform init
terraform plan -out=plan.tfplan
terraform show -json plan.tfplan | jq '.resource_changes[] | select(.change.actions | index("create") or index("delete"))'
```

matt: can you drop the PR link? i'll try to do a plan with my creds and check alias mappings
olivia: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/827 — main files: `root/providers.tf`, modules/*/remove-provider.tf, update to .terraform.lock.hcl. ping for reviews appreciated :eyes:
devops-bot: plan pipeline queued for branch refactor/hoist-providers — job 4321 :gear:
samir: one more, post-merge we should run `terraform providers mirror` and update our internal provider mirror for air-gapped clusters to avoid surprises
olivia: added a follow-up todo and updated the infra runbook. i'll wait for 2 approvals before merging. thanks all :thumbsup:
